facts.statement: The genus Cyclobatis was described by Egerton in 1844.
Cyclobatis belongs to the extinct family Cyclobatidae.
Three species are recognized within the genus: Cyclobatis longicanudatus, Cyclobatis major, and Cyclobatis oligodactylus.
facts.quote: subdivision: *Cyclobatis longicanudatus Cyclobatis major Cyclobatis oligodactylus

facts.statement: The genus is characterized by a circular body shape.
facts.quote: The genus is typified by a circular form.

facts.statement: Cyclobatis had a very short tail equipped with a venomous stinger.
facts.quote: This fish had a very short tail, fitted with a venomous stinger.

facts.statement: Cyclobatis major could grow to a length of about 25 cm.
facts.quote: Cyclobatis major can reach a length of about 25 cm

facts.statement: Cyclobatis oligodactylus reached a length of around 15 cm.
Cyclobatis lived in warm, shallow seas during its lifetime.
facts.quote: In life the environment of this creature was a warm shallow sea.

facts.statement: Cyclobatis lived between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Cyclobatis is an extinct genus of stingray-like skate found in the Upper Cretaceous of modern-day Lebanon.
rejected.quote: Cyclobatis is an extinct genus of stingray-like skate from the Upper Cretaceous of what is now Lebanon.
